subject: EU partial routing blip — customer update and follow-up
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liza Moreno <liza.moreno@novaresearch.com>, ops@novaresearch.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:15:00 +0100
Subject: EU partial routing blip — immediate customer update

Hi Liza,

Short update from the platform team: we observed a partial routing misclassification affecting a subset of EU-hosted inference traffic that started at ~15:58 CET. For Novaresearch this manifested as elevated p95 latency on text-generation calls and a small number of streaming chunk stalls.

Impact:
- ~2.4% of requests routed to a constrained capacity path between 15:58–16:35 CET, resulting in p95 climbs (from ~480ms to ~1.9s) and occasional stalled streaming chunks.
- No data loss or model-output truncation detected.

Mitigation in progress:
- We have isolated the mislabelled routing rule in the control plane and are preparing a targeted rollback to restore normal routing for your affected pool.
- Temporary mitigation: traffic will be routed to the next-compatible pool with slightly higher cost but consistent latency.

What we’re doing next:
- Applying the routing rollback within the next 30–45 minutes; I will send an update when traffic normalizes.
- Full timeline and debug artifacts will be shared in a postmortem after we complete the triage.

Attachments: incident-timeline.pdf (summary timeline — initial draft).

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep this as brief and factual as possible.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:32:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU partial routing blip — immediate customer update

Jasmine — quick internal note.

We traced the cause to a newly deployed control-plane predicate that mis-evaluated a region tag for a small percentage of sessions (approx 2.4%). The predicate incorrectly matched traffic coming from the EU-eu1 pool and pushed it to a fallback routing tier that had limited capacity.

Action we are taking now:
- Rolling back the predicate in prod (control-plane) — rolling out now, expected completion in ~10–12 minutes.
- Increasing headroom on the fallback pool to absorb any remaining drift.
- Capturing a hop-by-hop trace (debug-trace.log) and generating a short incident timeline PDF for customers.

Will confirm once rollback completes.

—Marissa
Director, Runtime Operations

Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 17:10:00 +0100
Subject: Update: routing rollback completed, traffic normalized (EU)

Hi Liza and team,

Quick follow-up — the targeted rollback to the control-plane predicate completed at 16:52 CET and we observed traffic normalization by 16:55 CET. For Novaresearch specifically we see the following:

- Normalized p50/p95: p50 returned to ~460ms, p95 dropped to ~560ms by 16:58 CET.
- The fallback pool remains at slightly elevated headroom while we monitor for reoccurrence.
- No model outputs appear to have been truncated; we validated a sample set of long-form streaming calls.

Open items:
- We will ship a brief postmortem with root cause, timeline, and planned preventive changes within 24 hours.
- If you saw any customer-facing anomalies we should know about (errors, retries, or UX regressions), please reply with example request ids and timestamps so we can correlate.

Status page link: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/RI-4572-eu-routing-blip

Attachments: incident-timeline.pdf (updated).

Thanks for your patience — I’ll follow up tomorrow with a concise RCA and remediation plan.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liza Moreno <liza.moreno@novaresearch.com>, ops@novaresearch.com
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 09:42:00 +0100
Subject: Post-incident readout: RI-4572 (EU routing predicate) — root cause & next steps

Hi Liza,

Following up with the technical readout for yesterday’s event (RI-4572). TL;DR: a recently deployed control-plane route-matching predicate incorrectly treated a transient metadata label change as an explicit region override, causing a small subset of EU-origin requests to be routed to a constrained fallback pool.

Root cause (brief):
- A predicate rollout included a guard that checked for a label key that we occasionally populate via an internal enrichment job. Under a narrow timing window the enrichment job produced a short-lived label that matched the predicate’s pattern.
- The predicate lacked an explicit safelist for the EU-eu1 canonical tag; when the transient label appeared the predicate evaluated to true and diverted ~2.4% of traffic.

Impact summary:
- Incident window: 2026-12-02T15:58:00Z -> 2026-12-02T16:55:00Z (rollback completed 16:52 CET; traffic normalized by 16:55 CET).
- Affected customers: small percentage of EU-hosted requests; Novaresearch observed elevated p95 and some streaming stalls; no data loss.

Actions completed:
- Immediate: rolled back predicate; increased fallback pool headroom; verified traffic normalization.
- Near-term fixes (planned and already scheduled):
  - Add explicit safelist for EU canonical tags to the predicate (deploy next week).
  - Harden predicate evaluation to ignore transient enrichment labels (in progress, ETA 2026-12-10).
  - Add additional canary traffic checks for predicate changes (operational change).

Artifacts attached: debug-trace.log (scrubbed traces), incident-timeline.pdf (final), remediation-plan.docx (action items and owners).

If Novaresearch wants a brief 30-minute walkthrough of the timeline and mitigations, reply with availability and we’ll schedule.

Apologies again for the disruption. We’re treating this as high priority to avoid recurrence.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
